claims.text: Laser cladding an HEA composite coating containing WC particles can repair damaged surfaces of high-value components.
WC–HEA laser-cladded coatings will reduce hot cracking relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
WC–HEA laser-cladded coatings will increase surface hardness relative to traditional fusion-welding repairs and untreated surfaces.
WC–HEA laser-cladded coatings will improve wear resistance relative to traditional fusion-welding repairs and untreated surfaces.
WC–HEA laser-cladded coatings will improve corrosion resistance relative to traditional fusion-welding repairs and untreated surfaces.
WC particles embedded in the HEA matrix deflect or interrupt crack propagation.
Embedded WC particles locally enhance coating hardness.
The HEA matrix provides chemical stability.
The HEA matrix provides additional resistance to wear and corrosion.
The combination of crack interruption by WC and stability from the HEA matrix mitigates hot-cracking risk.
Traditional fusion-welding repairs and untreated surfaces tend to have lower hardness than the proposed coating.
Traditional fusion-welding repairs and untreated surfaces tend to have higher crack density than the proposed coating.
Traditional fusion-welding repairs and untreated surfaces have diminished performance under aggressive environmental conditions relative to the proposed coating.
Coating effectiveness depends on selecting an appropriate WC content.
Coating effectiveness depends on laser power, scan speed, and cooling rate.
Extremely high thermal loads may limit the coating's benefits.
Non-optimal WC dispersion may limit the coating's benefits.
The optimal WC concentration and processing parameters may vary with substrate composition and service conditions.
